guideTitle: Best Rice Cookers for Sushi Rice (2026)
metaTitle: Best Rice Cookers for Sushi Rice (2026)
metaDescription: Seven rice cookers compared for sushi rice: short-grain control, water ratio, fuzzy logic, sushi menus and capacity, from 3 cup mini units to 20 cup pots.
expertTake: The Zojirushi NS-TSC10 is the best rice cooker for sushi rice because its micom fuzzy logic keeps short grains intact and its keep-warm modes hold rice without drying. The COMFEE' Japanese Style 10 cup is the value pick with an explicit sushi program and a large pot. Anyone who makes sushi only a few times a year should skip premium cookers and use a basic cooker with a careful rinse and rest.
introParagraphs: Sushi rice is a short-grain rice cooked slightly firm and then seasoned with a vinegar mixture while still warm. That makes the cooking step unusually unforgiving: too much water produces mush that cannot hold a roll, and too little leaves hard centers. The cooker's job is to give a steady, even cook and a firm but tender grain.

This guide compares seven cookers for that job. We look at control type, sushi or white rice menus, capacity, keep-warm behavior and cleanup, using listing specs and general knowledge of how short-grain rice cooks. The things that matter most are even heat, a menu that suits short grains and a pot size that fits the way you cook.

products.name: Zojirushi NS-TSC10 5.5 Cup Micom Rice Cooker and Warmer
products.description:
The NS-TSC10 uses microcomputer fuzzy logic to adjust heat through the cycle, which matters for short grains that break easily if the boil is too violent. It offers automatic keep-warm, extended keep-warm and a reheating cycle, plus two delay timer settings. The clear coated stainless exterior wipes clean easily.

The tradeoff is cost and capacity. It is a premium cooker, and 5.5 cups uncooked is enough for a family or a modest sushi dinner, not a party. Fewer refinements than the Zojirushi NS-ZCC10 are on offer, though the fuzzy logic approach is the same.

Ownership is easy: wash the inner pan and lid, wipe the steam vent and keep the heating plate dry. Do not leave sushi rice on keep-warm for long periods, because even extended keep-warm dries delicate short grains. Regular sushi rice makers get the most out of this one. Its two delay timer settings are handy if you want rice ready when you walk in after work.
products.bestFor: Regular sushi makers who want consistent short-grain results.
pros: Micom fuzzy logic adjusts heat through the cycle

products.name: Zojirushi NS-ZCC10 Neuro Fuzzy Rice Cooker and Warmer 5.5 Cup
products.description:
The NS-ZCC10 adds neuro fuzzy logic and a spherical nonstick pan that promotes uniform heating. For sushi rice, even heat from all sides cooks the grains consistently and avoids a crusty bottom. It also has multi-menu selections, extended keep-warm and a reheat cycle.

Against the NS-TSC10 it offers the same capacity at the highest cost in this guide. The difference is finer control and a rounder pan rather than a different type of rice. Compared with the COMFEE' it is far more precise but far less spacious.

Ownership is simple. Wash the pan and inner lid, wipe the vent and use only the supplied paddle. If sushi rice is a weekly event, the extra control is worth the premium. Because the pan is spherical, the rice circulates more freely during boiling, which helps each grain cook evenly.
products.bestFor: Sushi enthusiasts who want the finest control.
pros: Neuro fuzzy logic with fine heat control
cons: Nonstick pan needs a soft paddle

products.name: COMFEE' Japanese Style Rice Cooker 10 Cup Fuzzy Logic
products.description:
The COMFEE' Japanese Style cooker is a large fuzzy logic unit with a smart six-step cooking process and 11 programs that include white rice, brown rice and sushi. It has an LED display, an auto keep-warm of up to 12 hours and a 24 hour delay timer. For a sushi dinner for six to eight, the 10 cup pot is the draw.

The tradeoff is brand and fineness of control. It does not have the decades of tuning behind a Zojirushi, so results may vary from batch to batch until you learn it. Capacity is almost twice that of the Zojirushi NS-TSC10 at a lower cost, but the logic is less proven.

Clean the inner pot and lid after use, and avoid long keep-warm periods for sushi rice. It is a strong value choice for large households and parties. Because it is the largest of the fuzzy logic cookers here, it also suits meal prep with brown rice and porridge.
products.bestFor: Large households and parties that need a sushi program.
cons: Nonstick pot needs a soft paddle

products.name: TOSHIBA Small Rice Cooker 3 Cup with LCD and 8 Functions
products.description:
The Toshiba is a small cooker with an LCD display and eight programmable functions including white rice, quick cook and brown rice. A moisture sensor tunes the temperature and cooking time, which helps with short grains that vary by brand.

The limit is size. Three cups uncooked makes enough for a sushi dinner for two or three, but not for rolls for a group. It does not list a dedicated sushi menu, so use white rice and reduce the water slightly. Compared with the COMFEE' it is cheaper and smaller.

Rinse the rice thoroughly, rest it, then cook. Wash the pot after use. It suits couples who make sushi occasionally. Its small size also makes it easy to store, which suits people who only cook sushi rice now and then.
products.bestFor: Couples who make sushi occasionally and want a compact cooker.

products.name: AROMA Digital Rice Cooker 4 Cup Uncooked with Steam Tray
products.description:
The AROMA Digital cooker has programmable controls and presets for white rice, brown rice, steam and flash rice, with an automatic keep-warm after each cycle. It includes a steam tray. For sushi rice, the white rice preset with a reduced water level can produce a good result when you are careful.

Being thermostat-based, it comes without fuzzy logic or a sushi menu. Cook quality depends on rinsing, resting and water measurement, and results can vary. Compared with the COMFEE' it has less control but a lower price.

Rinse the rice, rest it for 20 to 30 minutes and use slightly less water than the white rice line. Wash the pot and lid after use. It suits budget buyers who will tune the method. The steam tray is useful for cooking vegetables for fillings while the rice cooks below.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who will tune the water and rest time.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ERC003BX 3 Cup Rice Cooker
products.description:
The Elite Gourmet ERC003BX is a basic one-touch cooker with a nonstick aluminum inner pot and an automatic keep-warm mode. It cooks 3 cups uncooked and also handles soups, stews and grains. For occasional sushi rice, it works when you manage the water yourself.

Nothing here is simpler: no fuzzy logic, no sushi menu and no timer. Short grains can get a firm crust at the bottom if the pot sits on keep-warm. Compared with the Toshiba it has fewer functions, but it costs less.

Rinse and rest the rice, measure the water carefully and switch to a bowl soon after cooking. It is the least expensive way to try sushi rice at home. Its light aluminum pot also heats quickly, so cooking times are short for small batches.
products.bestFor: Occasional sushi makers who want the lowest outlay.
cons: No fuzzy logic or sushi menu

products.name: Aroma Professional Plus ARC-5000SB 20 Cup Digital Rice Cooker
products.description:
The ARC-5000SB is a large digital cooker with a 20 cup cooked capacity, a food steamer and a slow cooker function. It yields anywhere from 4 to 20 cups of cooked rice, which suits parties and sushi nights. The stainless body is easy to wipe clean.

The compromise is control. Like the other Aroma cookers it is thermostat based, so it does not have the heat-curve finesse of a fuzzy logic cooker. Large batches also take longer to rest and cool for sushi, and a big pot can leave a firm layer at the bottom. Compared with the COMFEE' it has the same rough capacity but fewer rice-specific programs.

Rinse and rest the rice well, and spread it on a wide tray to cool before seasoning. It suits families and events where volume matters most. Because it is big, make sure the counter has enough clearance above for steam when the lid opens.
products.bestFor: Parties and large families that need big batches.
cons: Big batches can crust at the bottom

buyingCriteria.explanation: Sushi rice is short grain, which holds more starch at the surface and breaks if boiled hard. A fuzzy logic cooker like the Zojirushi NS-TSC10 or COMFEE' eases the heat through the cycle. A basic thermostat cooker like the Elite Gourmet ERC003BX heats at full power until the pot gets hot, which is harder on delicate grains. If the grains look blown open and the water is cloudy, the cooker is boiling too hard.

Short grain for sushi usually takes close to a 1 to 1 ratio of rice to water by volume, a little less than ordinary rice, because you want it firm. Rinse until the water runs mostly clear, then rest the rice for 20 to 30 minutes before cooking. Cookers with a sushi menu adjust this for you. Basic cookers rely on your method. Weigh or measure the rice with the same cup each time so that batches match.

The COMFEE' lists sushi among 11 programs, and the Zojirushi cookers offer multiple menus. A sushi menu makes the rice slightly firmer and drier, which suits seasoning with vinegar. Without it, use white rice with a little less water, and test one batch before a dinner party. Always check the manual to see whether the sushi program already includes a built-in soak.

A 3 cup cooker like the Toshiba or Elite Gourmet makes six cups cooked, enough for about three to four rolls. A 5.5 cup Zojirushi is a family size. The COMFEE' at 10 cups and the Aroma Professional Plus at 20 cups cooked suit parties. Do not overfill, as starch foam can climb into the vent. Make slightly more than you think you need, because rice cools and shrinks quickly.

Sushi rice should be moved out of the cooker once it is cooked, because the vinegar seasoning is applied while the rice is still warm. Keep-warm dries and yellows rice on simple cookers, while the Zojirushi models offer extended keep-warm and reheat. Even so, do not rely on keep-warm for sushi. Spread the hot rice thinly in a wide bowl and fan it as you season.

Short-grain rice leaves a starchy film. Nonstick pots like the Toshiba and Elite Gourmet release it easily but need soft paddles. A worn coating sticks and chips. Wash the lid and steam vent after each cook, and replace the pot if it flakes. If the nonstick coating starts to flake, stop using the pot, since flakes can end up in the rice.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control type
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared fuzzy logic cookers against thermostat cookers, favoring fuzzy logic for short grains.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sushi suitability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for sushi menus and short-grain friendly cycles, found on the COMFEE' and in the Zojirushi menus. We also considered whether the listing mentions short-grain or Japanese-style rice.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity spread
howWeEvaluated.description: We covered 3, 4, 5.5, 10 and 20 cup models, from two people to parties.

howWeEvaluated.title: Keep-warm and finishing
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted extended keep-warm and reheat on the Zojirushi cookers, and the drying risk on basic models. We treated any keep-warm longer than a few hours as a risk for delicate rice.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleanup and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed coatings, removable lids and steam vents, which matter for sticky short-grain rice.

rows: Fuzzy logic at a moderate cost

cards.label: Fuzzy logic (Zojirushi, COMFEE')
cards.text: Adjusts heat as the rice cooks and is gentler on short grains. It costs more but gives more repeatable sushi rice.

cards.label: Thermostat (Aroma, Elite Gourmet, Toshiba)
cards.text: Heats at full power until the pot gets hot and then switches off. Cheap and simple, but it needs careful water measurement.

howToChoose.note: Pick fuzzy logic if you make sushi often, and a thermostat cooker if you do it a few times a year.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A gentle heat curve, a sushi or white rice menu that cooks slightly firm and a pot you can empty quickly. Plan to season the rice while still warm in a wide bowl.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The COMFEE' has an explicit sushi program, and the Zojirushi NS-TSC10 gives the most consistent short-grain cook.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You make sushi weekly and want repeatable rice. The Zojirushi NS-TSC10 or NS-ZCC10 pays back in consistency.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You make sushi occasionally. A basic Aroma or Elite Gourmet cooker works with a careful rinse and rest.

maintenance.task: Rinse the pot after every cook
maintenance.why: Starch dries into a film that is hard to remove. A quick rinse prevents it.

maintenance.task: Wash the lid and steam vent
maintenance.why: Starch residue breeds odors and clogs vents.
Grains under the pot cause uneven heating and failed shut-off.
Metal scratches nonstick pots and shortens their life.
Flaking or scratches mean it is time to replace the pot.

faq.q: What rice do I use for sushi?
faq.a: Use a short-grain rice sold for sushi. Rinse it until the water is mostly clear, then rest it before cooking. Look for packages labeled sushi rice or short-grain Japanese rice.

faq.q: How much water do I use?
faq.a: About 1 to 1 by volume for short grain, a little less than regular rice. Adjust by small amounts after a first batch.

faq.q: Can I leave the rice on keep-warm?
faq.a: Not for sushi. Season the rice while it is still warm and move it out of the cooker. Leaving it warm dries the surface and makes the grains stiff.

faq.q: Do I need a sushi menu?
faq.a: It helps but is not required. A basic cooker with careful water measurement can make good sushi rice.
If you make sushi often, yes. It gives more repeatable texture than a basic thermostat.

faq.q: How big a cooker should I buy?
faq.a: Three cups uncooked suits two people. Five and a half cups suits a family and 10 cups suits parties. Choose the size that matches your largest typical batch.
